title: John Chrysostom on Jonah 1:3
body: “But if they be themselves dumb, how did they give responses to others? And wherefore did the demon lead them to the images?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “Pero si ellos mismos son mudos, ¿cómo daban respuestas a otros? ¿Y por qué el demonio los llevaba a las imágenes?”

title: Jerome on Jonah 1:4
body: “Jonah, fairest of doves, whose shipwreck shews in a figure the passion of the Lord, recalls the world to penitence, and while he preaches to Nineveh, announces salvation to all the heathen.”
author: Jerome, Letter 53, to Paulinus
bodyEs: “Jonás, la más hermosa de las palomas, cuyo naufragio muestra en figura la pasión del Señor, llama al mundo al arrepentimiento y, mientras predica a Nínive, anuncia la salvación a todos los gentiles.”

title: John Chrysostom on Jonah 1:7
body: “And they appointed two," it is said. Why not many? That the feeling of disappointment might not reach further, extending to many.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans
bodyEs: “Y designaron a dos", se dice. ¿Por qué no a muchos? Para que el sentimiento de decepción no llegara más lejos, extendiéndose a muchos.”

title: John Chrysostom on Jonah 3:4
body: “Thus, in the case of material leaven, the unleavened might become leavened, but never the reverse; whereas here there is a chance of the direct contrary occuring. This however he has not plainly declared: and observe his good sense.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “Así, en el caso de la levadura material, lo sin levadura podría volverse leudado, pero nunca al revés; mientras que aquí hay posibilidad de que ocurra lo directamente contrario. Esto, sin embargo, no lo ha declarado con claridad: y observa su buen sentido.”

title: John Chrysostom on Jonah 3:4
body: “I have not said these things without an object, nor am I making lamentations to no purpose, but with the view that one and all, with our women and children, having sprinkled ourselves with ashes, and girded ourselves about with sackcloth, may keep a long fast, may beseech God Himself to stretch forth His hand to us, and to stay the peril. For need is there indeed of His hand, that mighty, that marvelous hand.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “No he dicho estas cosas sin objeto, ni hago lamentaciones en vano, sino con el fin de que todos y cada uno, con nuestras mujeres y niños, habiéndonos rociado de ceniza y ceñido de cilicio, guardemos un largo ayuno, y roguemos a Dios mismo que nos extienda su mano y detenga el peligro. Porque en verdad se necesita su mano, aquella mano poderosa, aquella mano maravillosa.”
